From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>

Subject: Post-call: Model fit & eval next steps for PayGrid

Alex — thanks for the call and the clear use-case breakdown. Recap + recommended next steps below.

Recap (quick)
- Scope: transaction intent classification, entity extraction (payee/name/amount), short reply generation for merchants
- Data: PayGrid will run Redwood's prompt sets against withheld labeled slice (~2k examples) and share aggregated results; Redwood will provide eval harness and analysis dashboards
- Success criteria: parity on quality metrics (see thresholds below) with acceptable latency and cost targets

Recommended open models to evaluate (order = priority for first runs)
- LLaMA 2 (13B) — good baseline for instruction-following, lower cost than larger 40B variants
- Mistral-Instruct (7B) — strong for instruction tasks and often good for classification with tuned prompts
- Falcon 40B (instruction-tuned flavor) — to test upper-end open-model quality for generation/complex entity extraction

Suggested evaluation metrics & parity thresholds
- Transaction intent (multi-class accuracy / macro-F1): target parity >= 95% of PayGrid-Baseline v2 (i.e., if baseline accuracy = 0.92, target >= 0.874)
- Entity extraction (NER F1): absolute target F1 >= 0.90 or >= 95% of baseline (whichever is higher)
- Reply generation (BLEU/ROUGE + human quality pass rate): aim for human pass rate >= 90% of baseline on a 200-sample blind eval
- Latency: median generation latency for reply generation SLO < 250ms per token (quantized/optimized path target)
- Cost: expected per-call cost not to exceed 40% of baseline cost after batching/quantization recommendations

Attachments & links (first drop)
- paygrid_eval_promptset_v2.csv (prompt variations / canonical examples) — attached
- benchmark_results_20260519.pdf — template report we will populate after the first runs
- Colab/benchmark harness link: https://colab.research.google.com/drive/1paygrid-benchmark-notebook
- Shared Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-paygrid-evals

Next steps
1) PayGrid: run the promptset against your withheld labeled slice and upload aggregated outputs (no raw PII) to shared drive folder by Tue 5/19 EOD
2) Redwood (Aditya): run first-pass evals on the three recommended open models, produce the benchmark_results_20260519.pdf and share redlines with notes on prompt tweaks and quantization options (ETA Wed 5/20 noon PT)
3) Joint: schedule a 30-min follow-up to review parity and decide whether to (a) iterate on prompts, (b) run a blind human eval, or (c) explore proprietary model fallback. Proposed time slots attached in the calendar invite.

If that all looks good, we'll proceed. Quick note: if open models hit parity within thresholds, we can discuss Dedicated/private deployment cost estimates and an initial pilot.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
To: Priya Singh <priya.singh@paygrid.com>; Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>; Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@paygrid.com>
Date: Tue, 19 May 2026 11:45:30 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: Model fit & eval next steps for PayGrid

Priya — good questions. Short answers + technical notes:

Quantization & infra recommendations
- For the first pass we recommend 4-bit quantization (GPTQ-style) on LLaMA 2 13B and Mistral 7B; that gives a strong cost/latency tradeoff for classification and short generation tasks. For Falcon 40B we'll run a quantized variant and a float16 variant to compare quality delta.
- VM/GPU suggestions: A single A10G or A100s-v4 instance per model shard for initial runs (batching enabled). For dedicated pilot, we recommend 2x A10G with an autoscaling policy for peak traffic patterns.

PII / data handling
- Please only upload aggregated outputs (predictions + example ids). Do not upload raw logs or raw PII. Redwood can run the benchmark in your VPC/private deployment if you'd prefer; otherwise we accept sanitized output CSVs. We'll sign an NDA/data processing addendum if needed.

Parity history (what we've seen)
- We've repeatedly seen open models hit parity on structured classification tasks (intent, routing, simple NER) when properly prompt-tuned and when using a small calibration set (~500 labeled examples).
- For complex extraction and nuanced generation, larger open models or quantized+FT/LoRA approaches are sometimes required to match a well-tuned proprietary baseline. In one recent customer pilot (payments vertical), LLaMA 2 13B + prompt engineering + simple LoRA reached ~97% of the baseline F1 on NER and matched intent accuracy within 3 points after 3 iterations.

Proposed gating / evaluation plan
- Phase 1 (automated): Redwood runs the recommended models against your outputs and reports automated metrics (accuracy, F1, latency, cost). If any open model is within the parity thresholds we defined, proceed to Phase 2.
- Phase 2 (blind human eval): 200-sample blind eval with PayGrid reviewers (preferred) + Redwood QA coordinator. We'll provide rubric and manage the blindization. If you'd rather have Redwood use third-party annotators under an NDA, we can arrange that as well.

I'll start the first-pass runs as soon as you drop the aggregated outputs into the shared drive (and grant read access to aditya@redwood.com). Expect the PDF report by Wed 5/20 noon PT.

—Aditya
Senior ML Platform Engineer | Redwood Inference
